comment_text: I find these results quite logical given the fact that through WoE you force the univariate relationship of LN GB odds to points assigned while dummy variables approach lets the model optimize coefficients in the multivariable set up. With WoE you force more intervals/ variables into the model at the expense of accuracy, in the dummy approach you are accurate in your prediction for dummy =1 segments that enter the model but you are still not accurate for the ones that don't enter the model. I find usefulness in WoE where you want to get to a model quickly (e.g. you have many variables, you don't want to remove highly correlated before you build a model, you don't want to play with the classing, etc.) or you are struggling with granularity. Nevertheless dummy variables remains the more robust approach.
